title: Finite projective dimension of the residue field is at most the Krull dimension
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with residue field $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$, and let $\dim R\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ be its Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] (the supremum of the lengths $l$ of chains $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\dots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_l$ of prime ideals of $R$). If $\kappa$ has finite projective dimension as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], then $\operatorname{pd}_R\kappa\le\dim R$; in particular, if $\dim R$ is finite, $\kappa$ has a projective resolution of length $\le\dim R$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OB (lemma-dim-gl-dim, line 27072), with its proof (minimal finite free resolution via Lemmas what-kind-of-resolutions-Noetherian-local and add-trivial-complex; depth of the ideal of minors I(phi_n) >= n by Proposition what-exact (Buchsbaum-Eisenbud); depth <= dimension by Lemma bound-depth). Tag verified in tags/tags: 00OB,algebra-lemma-dim-gl-dim

proof.text: (A minimal finite free resolution.) By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-dimension-well-defined] (2) the projective dimension $d=\operatorname{pd}_R\kappa\ge0$ exists and $\kappa$ has a projective resolution of length $\le d$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$ is a finitely generated $R$-module (generated by the class of $1$) [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-finite-free-resolution-local] (Stacks 0CXF condition (7), with the reduction by 00MT used in the proof of 00OB) applied to $M=\kappa$ there is an exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] $0\to F_d\xrightarrow{\varphi_d}\cdots\xrightarrow{\varphi_1}F_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}\kappa\to0$ with $F_j\cong R^{\oplus n_j}$ finite free [def-weil-pbc-free-module] and every matrix coefficient of every $\varphi_j$ ($1\le j\le d$) in $\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00OB (lemma-dim-gl-dim, line 27072), first two sentences, citing Lemmas Tag 0CXF (lemma-what-kind-of-resolutions-Noetherian-local, line 26702) and 00MT (lemma-add-trivial-complex, line 24608)

Dropping the zero terms $F_j$, $j>n$, the sequence $0	o F_n	o\cdots	o F_0	o\kappa	o0$ is still exact (exactness at $F_n$, i.e. injectivity of $\varphi_n$, is exactness of the original sequence at $F_n$, since $F_{n+1}=0$ if $n<d$). Its terms are free, hence projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], so it is a projective resolution of length $\le n$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension] and $\operatorname{pd}_R\kappa\le n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-dimension-well-defined] (2). If $n=0$, then $\operatorname{pd}_R\kappa=0\le\dim R$, since $\mathfrak m$ is a prime ideal, a chain of length $0$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and we are done; assume $n\ge1$.

proof.text: (Buchsbaum-Eisenbud.) The complex $0\to R^{\oplus n_n}\xrightarrow{\varphi_n}\cdots\xrightarrow{\varphi_1}R^{\oplus n_0}$ of Step 2 is a complex of finite free modules over the Noetherian local ring $R$, with $n\ge1$, exact at $R^{\oplus n_n},\dots,R^{\oplus n_1}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-free-complex-last-minors-regular-sequence] (Stacks 00N1, (1) => (2)(b) for $i=n$), the ideal $I$ generated by the $n_n\times n_n$ minors of the matrix of $\varphi_n$ is either $R$ or contains an $R$-regular sequence of length $n$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00OB (lemma-dim-gl-dim, line 27072), fourth sentence, citing Proposition Tag 00N1 (proposition-what-exact, line 24834)

proof.text: ($I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, so $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge n$.) Since $n_n\ge1$, each $n_n\times n_n$ minor is, by the Leibniz formula [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], a sum of $\pm$ products of $n_n\ge1$ coefficients of $\varphi_n$, each in $\mathfrak m$ by Step 1; so every minor lies in $\mathfrak m$ and $I\subseteq\mathfrak m\ne R$ ('$I(\varphi_n)$ cannot equal $R$ by our choice of the complex'). By Step 3, $I$ contains an $R$-regular sequence $f_1,\dots,f_n$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and $f_1,\dots,f_n\in I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. As $\mathfrak mR=\mathfrak m\ne R$, by the definition of depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] $\operatorname{depth}(R)=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(R)$ is the supremum of the lengths of $R$-regular sequences in $\mathfrak m$, hence $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge n$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00OB (lemma-dim-gl-dim, line 27072), fourth sentence

proof.text: (Depth bounds dimension; conclusion.) $R$ is a nonzero finite module over the Noetherian local ring $R$, so [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] (Stacks 00LK) gives $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(R)\ge\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge n$. Every prime $\mathfrak p$ lies in $\operatorname{Supp}(R)$: in $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], $1/1=0$ would need $u\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ with $u\cdot1=0$, impossible as $0\in\mathfrak p$; so chains of primes in $\operatorname{Supp}(R)$ are all chains of primes of $R$ and $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(R)=\dim R$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. With Step 2, $\operatorname{pd}_R\kappa\le n\le\dim R$. Finally, if $D=\dim R$ is finite, $\operatorname{pd}_R\kappa\le D$ and [lem-weil-pbc-projective-dimension-well-defined] (2) give a projective resolution of $\kappa$ of length $\le D$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension].

split_report.summary: Split following Stacks 00OB and its proof, read in algebra.tex lines 27072-27093 with the cited 0CXF (26702), 00MT (24608), 00N1 (24834), 00LK (17814). Five steps: (1) a finite free resolution of length pd with all matrix coefficients in m, from lem-weil-pbc-minimal-finite-free-resolution-local (0CXF + 00MT, created by the parallel item 00OA and cited, not duplicated); (2) pd <= n, the last nonzero index; (3) Buchsbaum-Eisenbud for the last map (new node lem-weil-pbc-exact-free-complex-last-minors-regular-sequence, 00N1 (1)=>(2)(b), i = e only); (4) the minors lie in m, so depth R >= n; (5) 00LK with M = R and Supp R = Spec R. Statement corrected: the clause 'in particular dim R is finite' does not follow (finiteness of dim R is Krull's theorem, which both citers take from lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-system-of-parameters); replaced by 'if dim R is finite, kappa has a projective resolution of length <= dim R'; stmt_deps gains def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring. Stacks' 'so that the projective dimension of kappa is n' is used only as pd <= n.
